title: Concurrent Suspense Resource Cache with Deduplication
concept: Resource Keying, Concurrent Request Deduplication & Invalidation
problemStatement: Implement `createSuspenseCache()` with `get(key, fetcher)` that deduplicates in-flight promises across concurrent suspended components, caches resolved results, and supports selective `invalidate(key)`.
interviewTrap: Without request deduplication in a shared Suspense cache, three child components suspending on the same user ID will fire three redundant network requests simultaneously.

testCases.name: Deduplicates multiple calls for identical key to single fetch invocation
testCases.testFn: const cache = createSuspenseCache(); let fetches = 0; const fetcher = () => { fetches++; return Promise.resolve(42); }; cache.get('u1', fetcher); cache.get('u1', fetcher); return fetches;

testCases.name: Invalidation causes subsequent call to fetch fresh data
testCases.testFn: const cache = createSuspenseCache(); let fetches = 0; const fetcher = () => { fetches++; return Promise.resolve(42); }; cache.get('u1', fetcher); cache.invalidate('u1'); cache.get('u1', fetcher); return fetches;

testCases.name: Suspends correctly on pending record
testCases.testFn: const cache = createSuspenseCache(); const record = cache.get('u2', () => new Promise(() => {})); try { record.read(); return false; } catch (p) { return p instanceof Promise; }

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: When a component suspends, it throws a Promise up the Fiber tree. React catches the promise, pauses the render phase for that branch, renders the nearest Suspense fallback, and resumes when the promise resolves.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Resource Keying, Concurrent Request Deduplication & Invalidation.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, Resource Keying, Concurrent Request Deduplication & Invalidation maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.

complexity.time: O(1) per hook / O(N) fiber traversal

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does React.cache deduplicate requests within a single render cycle?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: In React 18/19 Server Components, `React.cache(fn)` memoizes function calls based on argument identity for the duration of a single server request. If 5 different components call `getUser(id)` with the same `id` during the render pass, `getUser` executes exactly ONCE and the cached Promise is shared among all 5 components, eliminating duplicate network/database calls.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Core data architecture question for modern Next.js / React Server Components.

realWorldUseCases.description: Sharing database and fetch queries between layout.js, page.js, and metadata generators without prop drilling.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: export const getItem = cache(async (id) => db.item.findUnique({ where: { id } }));

howToExplain.opening: Suspense cache deduplication pools concurrent resource requests by key, sharing in-flight promises and caching resolved results.
keyPoints: Deduplicates in-flight requests made by multiple components.
Scoped to the lifetime of a single request in RSC.
Eliminates duplicate SQL/HTTP queries across component hierarchies.
Replaces manual prop drilling of fetched data.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Request deduplication allows components to fetch their own data independently without worrying about duplicate network requests.
analogies: A carpool: instead of 5 coworkers driving 5 cars to the same meeting, they all ride in the same car.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming React.cache persists across different user HTTP requests.
commonMistakes.why: React.cache is scoped strictly to a single request lifecycle; it is not a global Redis cache.
commonMistakes.correct: Clarify that cache is per-request to prevent cross-user data leaks.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does React.cache compare to TanStack Query (React Query)?
followUpDeepDive.answer: React.cache is built for Server Components during request rendering. TanStack Query manages client-side caching, background polling, mutations, and cache invalidation in the browser.
